security_audit.summary: All 19 static findings are false positives after context review. The hidden-directory entries are documented installation paths, the backtick hits are Markdown filename formatting, and the reconnaissance hits are benign marketing or review checklist text.

static_findings.snippet: Use the templates in `templates/` when a structured artifact is helpful:
Free skills can get hundreds of downloads while paid marketplaces still produce zero sales.
- Did the agent change files outside the expected scope?
- Did it invent a new abstraction when a local pattern already existed?
- Did it leave a manual step that should have been automated?
- Did it claim verification without showing the command or result?
- Did it expose secrets, tokens, private data, or account identifiers unnecessarily?

content.value_statement: Coding-agent projects can drift when tasks, scope, and checks are vague. This skill gives PM templates and review rules that keep Claude, Codex, and Claude Code work bounded and verifiable.
actual_capabilities: Defines an operating loop for assigning, validating, and reviewing coding-agent work.
Provides a PM agent brief template with outcome, scope, context, acceptance criteria, and review questions.
Includes task planning, prompt snippet, review checklist, and first-week workflow tracker templates.
Guides users to require validation commands, changed-file summaries, and remaining-risk reports.
Helps recover from scope drift by mapping agent changes back to the original acceptance criteria.
limitations: Does not implement code or run project validation commands by itself.
Does not connect to project management tools, issue trackers, or repositories.
Requires humans to provide accurate project context and inspect final diffs.
Does not replace security review for sensitive or regulated code changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a first agent task
use_cases.description: Create a clear brief with scope, context, acceptance criteria, and validation steps before a coding agent starts work.

use_cases.title: Review implementation work
use_cases.description: Check whether a completed agent change stayed in scope, met requirements, ran checks, and reported remaining risks.

use_cases.title: Coordinate parallel agent assignments
use_cases.description: Split implementation work into bounded tasks with separate file ownership, expected outputs, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic task brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one coding-agent task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use coding-agent-pm to turn this request into a short agent brief. Include the outcome, in-scope files, out-of-scope files, acceptance criteria, and validation commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a scoped implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert a feature request into a controlled work plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use coding-agent-pm to prepare an implementation plan for this feature. Keep the plan limited to the named modules, identify required context, and define checks the agent must run before final delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Review a completed agent change
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate an implementation before accepting it
prompt_templates.prompt: Use coding-agent-pm to review this agent result. Put findings first, compare the change against the original acceptance criteria, and list any missing checks, scope drift, or security and privacy risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design parallel agent assignments
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for multiple independent coding-agent tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use coding-agent-pm to split this project into independent coding-agent assignments. Give each task a disjoint write scope, expected output, acceptance criteria, validation commands, and a human review checkpoint.

output_examples.input: A founder wants an agent to add a small checkout improvement without touching unrelated pages.
output: A one-sentence shipped outcome for the checkout improvement.
An explicit list of files the agent may edit and files it must not edit.
Three acceptance criteria and the validation commands required before final delivery.

output_examples.input: A product manager needs to decide whether to accept an agent-completed bug fix.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a review checklist covering scope, behavior, code quality, verification, security, privacy, and remaining risks.

output_examples.input: A product engineer wants to split a larger feature across several agent sessions.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines separate assignments with owned files, expected outputs, validation steps, and review gates for each agent task.

best_practices: Name the shipped outcome, owned files, excluded files, and validation commands before implementation starts.
Require the final response to report changed files, checks run, results, and remaining risks.
Review the diff against acceptance criteria before asking for new edits or accepting the work.
anti_patterns: Giving a broad feature idea without ownership boundaries or acceptance criteria.
Accepting agent work that claims validation without showing the command and result.
Letting a coding agent keep expanding scope after it drifts from the original request.

faq.question: Which coding agents does this skill support?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and similar coding-agent workflows where a human owns scope and review.

faq.question: Does this skill write code for me?
faq.answer: No. It helps you plan, assign, review, and verify coding-agent work with better prompts and templates.

faq.question: Can it help when an agent changes too much?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes recovery guidance that asks the agent to stop, map changes to acceptance criteria, and identify out-of-scope edits.

faq.question: What templates are included?
faq.answer: It includes a PM agent brief, task plan, prompt snippets, review checklist, and first-week workflow tracker.

faq.question: Is this useful for non-technical PMs?
faq.answer: Yes. The templates use plain task, scope, and review language, but a technical reviewer should inspect code changes.

faq.question: Does it replace testing or code review?
faq.answer: No. It helps define required checks and review questions, but humans and project tests still validate the result.
